stem.en: Someone designs a wheel that, after one small push, should turn for ever and keep lifting a load. No such machine has ever worked. What is the best reason?

text.en: Friction and air take some energy at every turn, so it slows and stops.
Its parts wear out in time, and only that stops it.
It works, but its force is too small to be useful.
It fails only when the wheel is heavy; a light wheel would run for ever.

explanation.en: At every turn, friction and air resistance change some mechanical energy into heat and sound. Lifting a load also needs energy. Nothing puts this energy back, so the wheel slows down and stops. Wear is a separate problem; even a new machine stops.

hints.en: What do friction and air resistance do to mechanical energy?
Where would the energy to lift the load come from?
